mainEntity.name: Can a nontechnical founder build a real product with AI, or do I still need a developer?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A nontechnical founder can often direct early discovery and prototype work, but production software still needs someone capable of reviewing architecture, security, deployment, and maintenance. AI can reduce the barrier to expressing requirements; it does not remove technical responsibility.

For Run My AI Business readers, a lower-risk path may be to start with existing platforms and AI-assisted workflows before commissioning custom software. This can reveal whether the idea solves a real problem and which requirements are genuinely necessary.

Key factors:
- Sensitivity of customer and business data.
- Importance of uptime and accuracy.
- Complexity of integrations.
- Availability of ongoing technical support.

Practical guidance: Create a written scope and prototype, then obtain a technical review before handling payments, private information, or automated customer actions. Keep ownership of accounts, repositories, documentation, and deployment access.

Run My AI Business can help founders prepare clearer questions and workflows before they seek technical implementation help.
acceptedAnswer.description: AI can help a nontechnical founder plan and prototype, but important production software still needs technical review for security, architecture, deployment, and maintenance. Start with existing tools, document requirements, and obtain help before handling sensitive data or consequential actions.
